title: Standardize engineering artifacts across agents

summary.answer: Put the rule in Semantic contract. Prove it with one end-to-end path.
summary.context: Today skills/agent-artifacts/ and src/agent_artifacts/schemas/ each decide which sections an artifact must carry on their own.
summary.what_changes_it: Scenario regression lacks a required semantic section or fails visual review.

question: What must own this outcome so that it cannot happen: a required decision, risk, or validation step disappears because the generated layout changes.
answer: Semantic contract must own it, as the one explicit boundary. Caller-owned rules go once parity holds.
method: Read skills/agent-artifacts/ and src/agent_artifacts/mcp_server.py. Compare distributed, middleware, and explicit-boundary options.

findings.title: Distributed ownership keeps the failure
findings.claim: Every entry point repeats the rule, so one omission is enough: a required decision, risk, or validation step disappears because the generated layout changes.

evidence.detail: Plans, ADRs, reviews, and handoffs change structure and visual emphasis from one model session to the next.
Scenario regression lacks a required semantic section or fails visual review.

findings.implication: Semantic contract should own the rule, not help callers implement it.
findings.counterpoint: Centralization grows into a generic service unless its scope stays narrow.

findings.title: Reversibility beats immediate cleanup
findings.claim: The safest first release keeps the old path as rollback while outcomes are compared.

evidence.claim: The change crosses a shared boundary
evidence.detail: A rigid contract may make uncommon but legitimate document shapes difficult to express.

findings.implication: Removing compatibility code is its own milestone with one owner.
findings.counterpoint: Held too long, compatibility becomes a second supported architecture.

competing_views.limitation: Infers context and hides why a request failed

recommendations.recommendation: Make Semantic contract the single boundary
recommendations.why: Contains the failure and gives CLI and MCP adapters one output.
recommendations.next_test: Scenario regression lacks a required semantic section or fails visual review.

recommendations.why: Exposes missing context before callers depend on it.
